sentences.text: 2019 Indore, Dated 08.08.2019 Mr. Ankit Premchandani, learned counsel for the applicants.
Mr. Ankit Khare, learned counsel for the non- applicant/State.

Submissions were to be made on IA No.1000/2019 which is an application for suspension of sentence and IA No.2896/2019 which is an application for conversion of this criminal revision into criminal appeal.

Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that he does not want to press on application for suspension of sentence but he prays that this Criminal Revision be allowed and may converted into Criminal Appeal.

Considering this aspect, IA No.2896/2019 which is an application for conversion of criminal revision into criminal appeal, a perusal of provision of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'the Act of 2006') shows that against the order of Adjudicating Officer, an appeal lies before the Tribunal under Section 68(3) of the Act of 2006, the Adjudicating Officer has been shown to have the powers of a Civil Court.
Under Section 71 of the Act of 2006, the Tribunal has been shown to have powers of a Civil Court as well.

The applicants have filed this Criminal Revision in this matter and seeks to convert into Criminal Appeal but it must be pointed out that he has to challenge the order of Tribunal which has the trappings of a Civil Court, hence such orders can be challenged only on the Civil Side, therefore, the application for HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT INDORE CRIMINAL REVISION NO.650 OF 2019 conversion of Criminal Revision into Criminal Appeal is not acceptable.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants prays for time to file an appropriate application in this regard.
Let the matter be listed in the next week as prayed for.

(SHAILENDRA SHUKLA) JUDGE Arun/-
